name: Figma
tagline: Interface design and prototyping for product teams
description: Collaborative interface design and prototyping in the browser, with auto layout, developer handoff and AI features that shorten the path from idea to screen.
priceNote: Professional is $16 per full editor/month billed annually ($20 monthly); Organization is $55 per editor/month, annual billing only; Enterprise is quoted. Dev and Collab seats cost less than a full seat. Pricing as of October 2026; plans change — check the official site.
bestFor: Product designers and developers working on the same interface
pros: Real-time multiplayer with comments and version history keeps design and review in one file
Dev Mode and auto layout hand off spacing and specs that developers can actually use
The free Starter plan covers small teams, so you can test Figma with real project work
AI features such as layer renaming, copy drafting and layout suggestions cut the busywork
cons: Per-editor pricing split across Full, Dev and Collab seats gets confusing as headcount grows
Large files with thousands of frames become slow and memory hungry on older laptops
The free plan limits files and pages, which stops non-designers from exploring the tool
Heavy reliance on one proprietary file format creates real lock-in for agencies

features.name: Vector design and auto layout
features.detail: Constraint-based frames that resize without breaking the layout

features.name: Prototyping
features.detail: Interactive flows with variables, animations and conditional logic

features.name: Dev Mode
features.detail: Inspect specs, CSS and assets that developers can pull into code

features.name: AI assist
features.detail: Layer renaming, placeholder copy and layout suggestions in the canvas

features.name: Design systems
features.detail: Shared components, tokens and libraries for the whole organisation

features.name: Branching and history
features.detail: Explore directions in branches and restore any earlier state

useCases: Design a mobile app for a startup and hand the specs to developers the same day
Run a small agency client account from one shared file and a published design system
Prototype a landing page, test it with a handful of users and iterate before writing code
Keep marketing and product designers on the same components, tokens and spacing rules
bestForWho: Product design teams and small software shops that need collaborative UI design with clean developer handoff.
verdict: Figma remains the best place for a small product team to design, review and hand off an interface in one file. The auto layout system and Dev Mode are what actually change how design and engineering talk: developers stop reverse-engineering spacing and start reading real specs. The AI features are useful for the tedious layer of the job, like renaming a hundred inherited components, and less useful for the thinking part. The two things that frustrate people are price complexity and file performance, because a three-year-old file with thousands of frames drags on any machine. For design and product teams of two to thirty people, it is still the shortest path from idea to a shipped screen.
